atoms.text: This guide explains how to let the RelayGate load balancer service deliver access logs to a storage bucket through an IAM role. The role relaygate-log-writer and the bucket lb-access-logs-prod both belong to account 111122223333. Because both resources share one account, the grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not changed. Attach a policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:cloud:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/relaygate/prod/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:cloud:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod. Set the role's trust policy so that the RelayGate service principal can assume it. In the RelayGate console, set the delivery destination to lb-access-logs-prod with the prefix relaygate/prod/ and select the role. RelayGate writes one compressed log object every five minutes for each load balancer node, named with the timestamp and node ID. After saving, request a test delivery and confirm that a test object appears under the prefix. The role needs no read or delete permissions, because RelayGate only writes objects.

The role's trust policy, set in account 111122223333, must let the RelayGate service principal assume it. In the RelayGate console, set the delivery destination to lb-access-logs-prod with the prefix relaygate/prod/ and select the role. RelayGate writes one compressed log object every five minutes for each load balancer node, named with the timestamp and node ID. After saving, request a test delivery and confirm that a test object appears under the prefix. The role needs no read or delete permissions, because RelayGate only writes objects.

This guide covers granting the TrailMark audit service access to a bucket that stores account activity records. The role trailmark-delivery and the bucket org-audit-records are both in account 111122223333. The grant is carried only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy stays as it is. Add statements to the role policy allowing storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on arn:cloud:storage:::org-audit-records/trailmark/events/* and on arn:cloud:storage:::org-audit-records/trailmark/digests/*. TrailMark writes event files hourly and reads the previous hour's digest file so it can chain the checksum into the new digest. Configure the trail so that its delivery role is trailmark-delivery and its destination prefix is trailmark/. Enable object versioning on the bucket so that overwritten digests remain recoverable. Run the trail's validation command after the first two delivery cycles to confirm that the digest chain is intact. Do not grant storage:DeleteObject to the role, since TrailMark never removes delivered records.

This guide describes how to give an IAM user access to a bucket so that a self-hosted NetPulse collector can upload network flow logs. The user svc-netpulse-export and the bucket flowlogs-archive are both in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the user, and no bucket policy change is made. The policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:cloud:storage:::flowlogs-archive/netpulse/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting the prefix to netpulse/. Create an access key pair for the user and store it in the collector's credential file with permissions limited to the collector's service account. The collector batches flow records into gzip files of up to 64 MB and uploads each one under a date-based key such as netpulse/2025/03/14/. Set the collector's upload interval to 10 minutes and its retry limit to five attempts. Confirm the setup by checking that the first batch appears in the bucket and that no upload errors are present in the collector's log. Rotate the access key every 90 days and update the credential file when you do.

This guide shows how to let the EdgeLens CDN service write edge access logs to a bucket with a separate prefix for each distribution. The role edgelens-log-role and the bucket cdn-edge-logs are both in account 111122223333. The grant comes only from the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not modified. In that policy, allow storage:PutObject on arn:cloud:storage:::cdn-edge-logs/dist-*/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of dist-*. EdgeLens creates one prefix per distribution ID, such as dist-a1b2c3/, and writes a log object for each 15-minute window. Choose the bucket-owner-enforced ownership setting so that delivered objects belong to the bucket's account and ACLs are disabled. Register the role in the distribution's logging settings and enable logging for each distribution that should deliver. Verify delivery by listing the bucket after 20 minutes and checking that each active distribution has a new object. Log objects use gzip compression and include fields for client IP, edge location, status code, and bytes sent.

This guide explains how to give a log-ingestion job read access to DNS query logs that the NameScope resolver service has already delivered to a bucket. The role dns-ingest-reader and the bucket resolver-query-logs are both in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, with no change to the bucket policy. The policy allows storage:GetObject on arn:cloud:storage:::resolver-query-logs/namescope/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the namescope/ prefix. NameScope writes query logs to this bucket in 5-minute files that are partitioned by zone ID and date. The ingestion job lists the prefix for the current date, downloads files it has not yet processed, and records the last processed key in its own state store. Configure the job to assume dns-ingest-reader through its compute environment's execution settings. Test the setup by running one ingestion cycle and confirming that the job reports the expected file count. The role does not need write permission, because the job never modifies or removes the log files.

This guide describes how to let the QueryVault managed database service export slow-query logs to a bucket using multipart uploads. The role queryvault-export and the bucket db-diagnostics are both in account 111122223333. The grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is unchanged. The policy must allow storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:cloud:storage:::db-diagnostics/slowlogs/*. QueryVault splits any export larger than 100 MB into 16 MB parts and completes the upload after the final part is written. Add the service principal for QueryVault to the role's trust policy so that the export task can assume the role. Set the instance's export destination to db-diagnostics with the prefix slowlogs/ and a retention of 14 days for local copies. Add a bucket lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after seven days to avoid orphaned parts. Start a manual export and check that the resulting object size matches the size reported in the task details.

This guide covers permissions for the RunLedger function platform to deliver execution logs to a bucket, where every upload must request server-side encryption. The role runledger-shipper and the bucket fn-exec-logs are both in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not edited. The policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:cloud:storage:::fn-exec-logs/runledger/* with a condition that the x-storage-encryption request header equals AES256. RunLedger writes logs under keys of the form runledger/year/month/day/hour/function-name.log.gz. Each upload carries the encryption header, so requests that omit it are denied with an access error. Associate the role with the platform's log export setting and select fn-exec-logs as the destination. Invoke a test function and wait for the hourly flush to see its log file in the expected hourly folder. If the file does not appear, check the platform's delivery error log for access-denied entries that name the missing condition.

This guide describes how to let the GuardLine firewall service deliver traffic logs to a bucket and verify the destination during setup. The role guardline-log-writer and the bucket fw-traffic-logs are both in account 111122223333. The grant is carried only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. The policy allows storage:PutObject and storage:DeleteObject on arn:cloud:storage:::fw-traffic-logs/guardline/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of guardline/. When you save the destination, GuardLine writes a small probe object named guardline/.probe and then deletes it to confirm write access. During normal operation, GuardLine writes one log object per firewall instance every ten minutes under guardline/instance-id/. Specify the role and bucket in the firewall's logging configuration and set the log format to JSON lines. Confirm that the save operation reports a successful probe and that the first log object appears within 15 minutes. If the probe fails, review the role's policy for the exact bucket name and prefix.
